newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories up, sales down in March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories up, sales down in March.

text.p: Inventories held by businesses rose again in March, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday, but sales eased at all levels of manufacturing, wholesale and retail activity.

Total business inventories rose 0.3 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted $1.02 billion after a revised 0.4 percent jump in February, the department said. Previously, the department said inventories had risen only 0.3 percent in February.
The report fit with other signs of a tapering off in demand, including Tuesday's report from Commerce showing a 0.3 percent decline in retail store sales during April.
Total business sales in March fell 0.3 percent to a seasonally adjusted $743.99 billion after a 1.4 percent surge during February to $746.24 billion.
March inventories were higher at all stages of business and sales were similarly weaker, strongly suggesting the addition to unsold goods was involuntary.

March retail inventories increased 0.2 percent to $316.51 billion while manufacturers' stocks grew by 0.2 percent to $442.73 billion. Wholesale inventories rose 0.7 percent in March to $259.89 billion.

On the sales side, retail businesses posted a fractional decline in business to $212.97 billion. Manufacturers' sales declined 0.1 percent to $321.15 billion while wholesale sales were off 0.9 percent to $209.88 billion.

The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- climbed to 1.37 months' worth in March from 1.36 months' worth of stocks on hand in February.
